**SAA Research Standards Manual — Draft v4.2**

**Research Standards Committee**
**Singapore Archives and Records Association (SARA)**

**Document control**

**Distribution:** Committee members only. This draft is not for circulation outside the Committee until the endorsement vote is recorded.

---

**1. Purpose and scope**

1.1 This manual sets out the methodological standards for research conducted under the auspices of the Singapore Archives and Records Association (SARA), including studies undertaken by staff, affiliated researchers, and student interns whose work draws on SARA collections or facilities.

1.2 The standards apply to all stages of a research project: proposal design, data collection, citation practice, preservation of research records, and dissemination of findings.

1.3 Nothing in this manual overrides statutory obligations under the National Archives of Singapore Act or the Personal Data Protection Act 2012. Where a conflict arises, the statutory requirement prevails.

**2. Version history and status of this draft**

2.1 The Research Standards Committee maintains a single authoritative version of this manual. The current version is 4.2. SAA Research Standards Manual current_version 4.2 version. Record status: current. This draft, marked v4.2, is the version that the Committee will consider for endorsement at its December meeting. If endorsed without amendment, the v4.2 text will become the operative standard on 1 January 2024. If amendments are adopted, the Committee will issue a revised draft v4.3 before the end of the first quarter of 2024.

2.2 Superseded versions are retained in the Committee’s records for audit purposes. Researchers who rely on an older version for an active project must record that fact in their research log and note the version number in their final report.

**3. Changes introduced in this draft (v4.2)**

3.1 The following changes have been incorporated since v4.1:

(a) Section 5.4 (Oral history interviews) now requires interviewers to obtain written consent for the deposit of recordings in a public repository, in addition to consent for the interview itself.

(b) Section 7.2 (Citation of unpublished records) has been expanded to include guidance for citing records held in private hands and for citing digital surrogates held by SARA.

(c) Section 9.1 (Research records retention) now states a minimum retention period of five years for research data, with an exception for projects involving personal data, which must follow the retention schedule in Appendix C.

(d) A new Section 11 (Use of artificial intelligence tools) has been added. The Committee invites comment on whether the proposed safeguards are proportionate.

3.2 Margin annotations on this draft are those of the named reviewers. They are advisory only and will be discussed at the December meeting.

**4. Definitions**

For the purposes of this manual:

"Archival record" means a record, in any format, that is created or received by a person or organisation in the course of practical activity and preserved because of its continuing value.

"Research records" means the raw data, field notes, interview recordings, consent forms, correspondence, and analytical files generated during a research project.

"Researcher" means any person conducting research under SARA auspices, including staff, affiliated researchers, and interns.

"SARA collections" means the records, publications, oral history recordings, photographs, and other materials held by SARA or deposited with SARA for research use.

5.5 Observation and ethnographic methods

(a) Where research involves observation of individuals or communities, researchers shall obtain informed consent from participants in accordance with the ethical principles set out in Section 6.

**6. Ethical Considerations**

6.1 General principles

(a) Research conducted under SARA auspices shall be carried out with due regard for the dignity, privacy, and welfare of individuals and communities affected by the research.

(b) Researchers shall comply with all applicable laws and regulations, including the Personal Data Protection Act 2012 and any guidelines issued by the National Archives of Singapore.

6.2 Informed consent

(a) Informed consent shall be obtained from all participants in research involving human subjects, except where the Committee has granted an exemption in writing.

(b) The consent process shall be documented, and the consent forms shall be retained in accordance with Section 9.

6.3 Confidentiality and privacy

(a) Researchers shall take appropriate measures to protect the confidentiality of personal data obtained during research.

(b) Where personal data are to be published or otherwise disclosed, researchers shall obtain the consent of the data subject, or shall anonymise the data to the extent that the data subject cannot be identified.

(c) Researchers shall be mindful of the sensitivity of certain categories of personal data, including data relating to health, religion, and political opinion, and shall handle such data with particular care.
(a) Where a researcher has used an online finding aid or catalogue to identify a record, the finding aid itself shall be cited separately from the record, unless the finding aid entry contains the full reference for the record.

(b) The date of consultation of the online finding aid shall be included in the citation.

7.5 Examples

(a) The following examples illustrate the format set out in Section 7.2(a):

National Archives of Singapore, Straits Settlements Records, 1/S/10, File 123/45, p. 3, 12 March 1924.

NAS, Oral History Interviews, Accession No. 002456, Interview with Lee Kim Chuan, 15 July 1985, Track 2.

(b) Where a record is held in a repository outside Singapore, the repository name shall be given in full, for example:

The National Archives (United Kingdom), Colonial Office Records, CO 273/500, Despatch No. 42, 5 May 1931.

7.6 Consistency of citation practice

(a) Researchers shall adopt a single citation style for each piece of work and shall apply that style consistently throughout.

(b) Where a work draws on records from more than one repository, the researcher shall ensure that the citations for each repository are internally consistent and that the repository names are not abbreviated in a way that could cause confusion.

(c) Any deviation from the format set out in this Section shall be justified in the methodology note or preface to the work.

---

**Section 8. Publication and Dissemination of Research Findings**

8.1 General principles

(a) Researchers shall make their findings available to the scholarly community and to the public in a timely manner, unless the Committee has granted an exemption for reasons of confidentiality or sensitivity.

(b) Where findings are based on archival records, the researcher shall ensure that the citations conform to Section 7.

(c) Researchers shall not publish or otherwise disseminate personal data in contravention of Section 6.

8.2 Pre-publication review

(a) Where a researcher intends to publish findings that draw on records held by the National Archives of Singapore, the researcher shall submit the draft publication to the National Archives for review, where the records are subject to access conditions.

(b) The review shall be limited to verifying that the records are cited correctly and that no confidential or personal data are disclosed in contravention of the access conditions.

(c) The researcher shall allow a reasonable period for the review, not exceeding four weeks, unless the National Archives notifies the researcher of a longer period in writing.

8.3 Acknowledgement of archival sources

(a) In any publication arising from research conducted under SARA auspices, the researcher shall acknowledge the repositories consulted and the assistance of archivists and records managers, where appropriate.

(b) The acknowledgement shall not imply that the repository endorses the findings or conclusions of the work.

8.4 Deposit of research outputs

(a) Where a research project has been funded by SARA, the researcher shall deposit a copy of the final publication, and where practicable the underlying research data, with the SARA Library or the National Archives of Singapore, in accordance with the terms of the funding agreement.

(b) The deposit shall be made within three months of the date of publication.

**Section 9. Research Records Retention**

9.1 General principles

(a) Research records created or received in the course of SARA-funded or SARA-auspiced research shall be retained for a minimum of seven years after the conclusion of the research project, unless a longer period is required by law or by the terms of a funding agreement.

(b) For the purposes of this Section, “research records” include, but are not limited to: correspondence, field notes, interview recordings and transcripts, consent forms, laboratory notebooks, data files and databases, photographs, and drafts of publications.

(c) The researcher shall maintain research records in a manner that permits the reconstruction of the research process and the verification of published findings.

9.2 Location and custody

(a) Research records shall be kept in a secure location under the control of the researcher or the researcher’s institution.

(b) Where records are held by the National Archives of Singapore under a deposit agreement, the custody provisions of that agreement shall prevail.

9.3 Transfer on completion or departure

(a) Where a researcher leaves the institution or the research project concludes, the researcher shall arrange for the transfer of research records to the institution or to the SARA Library, as the case may be.

(b) The transfer shall be documented in a handover note, a copy of which shall be provided to the Research Standards Committee.

9.4 Disposal

(a) The disposal of research records shall be carried out in accordance with the institution’s records management policy and with any applicable legal requirements.

(b) Records containing personal data shall be disposed of in a manner that prevents the disclosure of that data.

(c) Where the National Archives of Singapore has expressed an interest in acquiring records, the researcher shall offer the records to the National Archives before disposal.

**Section 10. Citation Practices**

10.1 Purpose

This Section sets out the citation conventions to be followed in publications and other research outputs that draw on archival records. The conventions are intended to enable readers to locate the cited records with reasonable ease and to support the verification of research findings.

10.2 Minimum elements of a citation

(a) A citation to an archival record shall include the following elements, where they exist:

(i) the name of the repository;

(ii) the accession number or reference code of the record;

(iii) the title or description of the record;

(iv) the date or date range of the record; and

(v) the file or item number, where applicable.

(b) Where the record is held in a private collection, the citation shall also include the name of the owner of the collection and, where permitted, the owner’s contact details.

10.3 Order of elements

The elements listed in Section 10.2(a) shall appear in the order set out above. A comma shall separate the repository name from the reference code, and a full stop shall conclude the citation.

Example:

National Archives of Singapore, “Minutes of the Colonial Secretary’s Meetings, 1921–1923,” CO 273/521, f. 14.

10.4 Citations to digital records

(a) Where a record is consulted in digital form, the citation shall include the URL or persistent identifier and the date on which the record was accessed.

(b) Where a record is available only in digital form, the citation shall state that the record is a digital surrogate and, where known, the location of the original.

2.4 "Reading room" — the physical spaces designated for consultation of original and microfilmed records.

**3. ACCESS TIERS**

3.1 Access to SAA collections is organised into three tiers:

| Tier | Description | Examples | Registration Required |
|------|-------------|----------|----------------------|
| A | Open access — no registration | Published guides, indexes, publicly available finding aids, exhibition materials | No |
| B | Registered access — reading room use | Original records, microfilm, restricted digital databases | Yes (basic) |
| C | Controlled access — project-based | Records containing personal data, fragile originals, materials subject to donor restrictions | Yes (enhanced, with stated research purpose) |

3.2 Tier B registration is valid for two years from the date of issue. Tier C approvals are valid for a defined project period, not exceeding 12 months, and may be renewed once.

3.3 Applications for Tier C access must be submitted at least seven working days before the intended visit. The Access Review Panel will consider the research purpose, the sensitivity of the material, and the applicant's prior record of compliance.

**4. CLOSED MATERIAL**

4.1 The following categories of records are closed to public access:

a. Records containing personal data of living individuals, unless consent has been obtained or the records are more than 100 years old;

b. Records whose disclosure would prejudice the security of the Republic;

c. Records subject to a donor-imposed restriction;

d. Records whose physical condition makes consultation unsafe, pending conservation treatment.

4.2 The list of closed material is reviewed annually. Researchers may appeal a closure decision in writing to the Assistant Director (Access).

**5. READING ROOM USE**

SAA Public Access Protocol current_version 3.0 version. Record status: current.

5.1 Reading room hours are 9:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Mondays to Saturdays, excluding public holidays. The last admission is at 5:00 p.m.

5.2 All bags, briefcases, and personal devices must be deposited in the lockers provided on Level 1 of the Canning Rise building. Lockers are free of charge but require a $2 refundable deposit or a valid SAA access card.

5.3 Pencils and paper are permitted. Pens, markers, and correction fluid are not allowed in the reading room.

5.4 Researchers may request up to six items per visit. Items will be retrieved from the stacks and delivered to the assigned seat within 20 minutes.

5.5 No food or drinks, including capped water bottles, are permitted inside the reading room. A pantry with a water dispenser is located on Level 2, beside the lift lobby.

5.6 Photography of original records is permitted only where the item is not marked as "No Photography" and where flash is not used. Digital cameras and mobile phones may be used for this purpose, provided that the researcher has signed the Photography Agreement (Form PA-3).

**6. DIGITAL ACCESS SERVICES**

6.1 The SAA Online Catalogue is available at the public terminals in the reading room and remotely via the SAA website.

6.2 The following digital collections are available to Tier B researchers without further application:

a. Digitised photographs (pre-1965);

b. Colonial-era government gazettes;

c. Oral history interview summaries (access copies only);

d. Building plans index (metadata only).

6.3 Full audio and video recordings of oral history interviews are available only to Tier C researchers, subject to the conditions attached to each interview.
**8. CITATION AND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT**

8.1 All published work that draws on SAA collections must acknowledge the Singapore Archives Association and cite the specific record reference numbers used.

8.2 The recommended citation format is: “Singapore Archives Association, [record reference], [series title], [date].” Full citation guidance is provided in the SAA Style Sheet for Researchers, available at the reference desk.

8.3 Researchers are required to deposit one copy of any published work that is based substantially on SAA material, within three months of publication. This copy is held for reference use only.

**9. DATA PROTECTION AND PERSONAL INFORMATION**

9.1 Records containing personal data are subject to the Personal Data Protection Act 2012 and to any access restrictions imposed at the time of transfer.

9.2 Researchers who encounter personal information that is not relevant to their stated research purpose must not record, copy, or disclose that information.

9.3 Where a researcher believes that a record contains information that should be restricted under this Protocol, they may flag the item to the Assistant Director (Access) using Form FL-2. The flag does not itself close the record, but prompts a review within 14 working days.

**10. REVIEW AND AMENDMENT**

10.1 This Protocol is reviewed annually by the Public Access Working Group. Amendments are made by the Director (Collections) on the recommendation of the Group.

10.2 Proposed amendments are circulated to staff at least two weeks before the review meeting. Staff may submit comments in writing or attend the meeting.

10.3 Approved amendments are published as a revised version of the Protocol. The version number and date of approval are recorded on the cover page.

**11. APPROVAL AND EFFECTIVE DATE**

11.1 This version of the Public Access Protocol (Version 3.0) was approved by the Director (Collections) on 28 February 2024. SAA Public Access Protocol approved_date 2024-02-28 date. Record status: current.

11.2 The Protocol takes effect on 1 March 2024. Previous versions are superseded and are retained in the internal policy archive for reference only.

11.3 Staff are responsible for familiarising themselves with the provisions of this Protocol and for applying them consistently.

**2. Scope**
The guidelines apply to all engagement activities organised by SAA, including but not limited to
workshops, exhibitions, heritage trails, school visits, public talks, and digital outreach
initiatives.

**3. Key Principles**
3.1 Engagement should be inclusive and accessible to all members of the community, including
persons with disabilities, seniors, and families with young children.
3.2 Activities should be designed in consultation with community partners and participants where
practicable.
3.3 All engagement should reflect SAA’s commitment to preserving and promoting Singapore’s
archival heritage.

**4. Planning and Approval**
4.1 All engagement activities must be submitted for approval using the standard Activity Proposal
Form (APF-2024).
4.2 Proposals should be submitted at least four weeks before the proposed activity date.
4.3 The Director’s Office will review proposals and provide feedback within five working days.
4.4 Activities requiring significant resources or involving external partners must be endorsed by
the Director before commitment.

**5. Community Partners and Venues**
5.1 SAA welcomes collaboration with schools, grassroots organisations, museums, and other heritage
institutions.
5.2 When selecting venues, preference should be given to accessible locations, including those
near MRT stations or with good bus connectivity.
5.3 For activities held in public spaces such as void decks or community clubs, organisers must
obtain the necessary permits from the relevant authorities.

**6. Communication and Promotion**
6.1 All promotional materials should include the SAA logo and contact details.
6.2 Language used in materials should be clear and simple, with translations provided where
appropriate.
6.3 Digital promotion should be scheduled across SAA’s official social media channels at least
two weeks before the activity.

**7. Evaluation and Reporting**
7.1 Organisers must submit a brief activity report within two weeks of the activity.
7.2 Reports should include participant numbers, feedback received, and lessons learned.
7.3 The Director’s Office will maintain a central log of all engagement activities for annual
review.

3.1 The Chairman pro tem formally declared that the Straits Ancestry Archive was founded on 1995-04-12, upon the adoption of the Constitution and By-laws. This date shall be recorded as the official founding date of the organisation for all administrative and archival purposes.

3.2 The meeting noted that the founding of the Archive was the culmination of a series of informal discussions among genealogists, historians, and family historians which had taken place since late 1993. The Chairman pro tem recorded his appreciation to all who had contributed to the preparatory work.

**SAA Research Standards Manual — Draft v4.2**

**Research Standards Committee**
**Singapore Archives and Records Association (SARA)**

**Document control**

**Distribution:** Committee members only. This draft is not for circulation outside the Committee until the endorsement vote is recorded.

---

**1. Purpose and scope**

1.1 This manual sets out the methodological standards for research conducted under the auspices of the Singapore Archives and Records Association (SARA), including studies undertaken by staff, affiliated researchers, and student interns whose work draws on SARA collections or facilities.

1.2 The standards apply to all stages of a research project: proposal design, data collection, citation practice, preservation of research records, and dissemination of findings.

1.3 Nothing in this manual overrides statutory obligations under the National Archives of Singapore Act or the Personal Data Protection Act 2012. Where a conflict arises, the statutory requirement prevails.

**2. Version history and status of this draft**

2.1 The Research Standards Committee maintains a single authoritative version of this manual. The current version is 4.2. SAA Research Standards Manual current_version 4.2 version. Record status: current. This draft, marked v4.2, is the version that the Committee will consider for endorsement at its December meeting. If endorsed without amendment, the v4.2 text will become the operative standard on 1 January 2024. If amendments are adopted, the Committee will issue a revised draft v4.3 before the end of the first quarter of 2024.

2.2 Superseded versions are retained in the Committee’s records for audit purposes. Researchers who rely on an older version for an active project must record that fact in their research log and note the version number in their final report.

**3. Changes introduced in this draft (v4.2)**

3.1 The following changes have been incorporated since v4.1:

(a) Section 5.4 (Oral history interviews) now requires interviewers to obtain written consent for the deposit of recordings in a public repository, in addition to consent for the interview itself.

(b) Section 7.2 (Citation of unpublished records) has been expanded to include guidance for citing records held in private hands and for citing digital surrogates held by SARA.

(c) Section 9.1 (Research records retention) now states a minimum retention period of five years for research data, with an exception for projects involving personal data, which must follow the retention schedule in Appendix C.

(d) A new Section 11 (Use of artificial intelligence tools) has been added. The Committee invites comment on whether the proposed safeguards are proportionate.

3.2 Margin annotations on this draft are those of the named reviewers. They are advisory only and will be discussed at the December meeting.

**4. Definitions**

For the purposes of this manual:

"Archival record" means a record, in any format, that is created or received by a person or organisation in the course of practical activity and preserved because of its continuing value.

"Research records" means the raw data, field notes, interview recordings, consent forms, correspondence, and analytical files generated during a research project.

"Researcher" means any person conducting research under SARA auspices, including staff, affiliated researchers, and interns.

"SARA collections" means the records, publications, oral history recordings, photographs, and other materials held by SARA or deposited with SARA for research use.

The researcher shall note this restriction in the research log and in the final report.

5.5 Observation and ethnographic methods

(a) Where research involves observation of individuals or communities, researchers shall obtain informed consent from participants in accordance with the ethical principles set out in Section 6.

(b) Researchers shall take care to protect the identity of participants where anonymity has been promised. Where anonymity cannot be guaranteed, this shall be explained to participants before consent is obtained.

(c) Field notes shall be recorded in a manner that distinguishes between observation, interpretation, and quotation. This distinction shall be maintained in any published work based on the field notes.

5.6 Quantitative methods

(a) Where quantitative methods are used, researchers shall describe the data collection procedures, the sample selection, and the statistical methods employed, in sufficient detail to allow replication.

(b) Researchers shall retain the underlying data and the analysis files in accordance with Section 9 (Research records retention).

(c) Where data are derived from archival records, researchers shall cite the records in accordance with Section 7.

**6. Ethical Considerations**

6.1 General principles

(a) Research conducted under SARA auspices shall be carried out with due regard for the dignity, privacy, and welfare of individuals and communities affected by the research.

(b) Researchers shall comply with all applicable laws and regulations, including the Personal Data Protection Act 2012 and any guidelines issued by the National Archives of Singapore.

6.2 Informed consent

(a) Informed consent shall be obtained from all participants in research involving human subjects, except where the Committee has granted an exemption in writing.

(b) The consent process shall be documented, and the consent forms shall be retained in accordance with Section 9.

6.3 Confidentiality and privacy

(a) Researchers shall take appropriate measures to protect the confidentiality of personal data obtained during research.

(b) Where personal data are to be published or otherwise disclosed, researchers shall obtain the consent of the data subject, or shall anonymise the data to the extent that the data subject cannot be identified.

(c) Researchers shall be mindful of the sensitivity of certain categories of personal data, including data relating to health, religion, and political opinion, and shall handle such data with particular care.

(b) The date of consultation of the online finding aid shall be included in the citation.

7.5 Examples

(a) The following examples illustrate the format set out in Section 7.2(a):

NAS, Oral History Interviews, Accession No. 002456, Interview with Lee Kim Chuan, 15 July 1985, Track 2.

(b) Where a record is held in a repository outside Singapore, the repository name shall be given in full, for example:

The National Archives (United Kingdom), Colonial Office Records, CO 273/500, Despatch No. 42, 5 May 1931.

7.6 Consistency of citation practice

(a) Researchers shall adopt a single citation style for each piece of work and shall apply that style consistently throughout.

(b) Where a work draws on records from more than one repository, the researcher shall ensure that the citations for each repository are internally consistent and that the repository names are not abbreviated in a way that could cause confusion.

(c) Any deviation from the format set out in this Section shall be justified in the methodology note or preface to the work.

---

**Section 8. Publication and Dissemination of Research Findings**

8.1 General principles

(a) Researchers shall make their findings available to the scholarly community and to the public in a timely manner, unless the Committee has granted an exemption for reasons of confidentiality or sensitivity.

(b) Where findings are based on archival records, the researcher shall ensure that the citations conform to Section 7.

(c) Researchers shall not publish or otherwise disseminate personal data in contravention of Section 6.

8.2 Pre-publication review

(a) Where a researcher intends to publish findings that draw on records held by the National Archives of Singapore, the researcher shall submit the draft publication to the National Archives for review, where the records are subject to access conditions.

(b) The review shall be limited to verifying that the records are cited correctly and that no confidential or personal data are disclosed in contravention of the access conditions.

(c) The researcher shall allow a reasonable period for the review, not exceeding four weeks, unless the National Archives notifies the researcher of a longer period in writing.

8.3 Acknowledgement of archival sources

(a) In any publication arising from research conducted under SARA auspices, the researcher shall acknowledge the repositories consulted and the assistance of archivists and records managers, where appropriate.

(b) The acknowledgement shall not imply that the repository endorses the findings or conclusions of the work.

8.4 Deposit of research outputs

(a) Where a research project has been funded by SARA, the researcher shall deposit a copy of the final publication, and where practicable the underlying research data, with the SARA Library or the National Archives of Singapore, in accordance with the terms of the funding agreement.

(b) The deposit shall be made within three months of the date of publication.

**Section 9. Research Records Retention**

9.1 General principles

(a) Research records created or received in the course of SARA-funded or SARA-auspiced research shall be retained for a minimum of seven years after the conclusion of the research project, unless a longer period is required by law or by the terms of a funding agreement.

(b) For the purposes of this Section, “research records” include, but are not limited to: correspondence, field notes, interview recordings and transcripts, consent forms, laboratory notebooks, data files and databases, photographs, and drafts of publications.

(c) The researcher shall maintain research records in a manner that permits the reconstruction of the research process and the verification of published findings.

9.2 Location and custody

(a) Research records shall be kept in a secure location under the control of the researcher or the researcher’s institution.

(b) Where records are held by the National Archives of Singapore under a deposit agreement, the custody provisions of that agreement shall prevail.

9.3 Transfer on completion or departure

(a) Where a researcher leaves the institution or the research project concludes, the researcher shall arrange for the transfer of research records to the institution or to the SARA Library, as the case may be.

(b) The transfer shall be documented in a handover note, a copy of which shall be provided to the Research Standards Committee.

9.4 Disposal

(a) The disposal of research records shall be carried out in accordance with the institution’s records management policy and with any applicable legal requirements.

(b) Records containing personal data shall be disposed of in a manner that prevents the disclosure of that data.

(c) Where the National Archives of Singapore has expressed an interest in acquiring records, the researcher shall offer the records to the National Archives before disposal.

---

**Section 10. Citation Practices**

10.1 Purpose

This Section sets out the citation conventions to be followed in publications and other research outputs that draw on archival records. The conventions are intended to enable readers to locate the cited records with reasonable ease and to support the verification of research findings.

10.2 Minimum elements of a citation

(a) A citation to an archival record shall include the following elements, where they exist:

(i) the name of the repository;

(ii) the accession number or reference code of the record;

(iii) the title or description of the record;

(iv) the date or date range of the record; and

(v) the file or item number, where applicable.

(b) Where the record is held in a private collection, the citation shall also include the name of the owner of the collection and, where permitted, the owner’s contact details.

10.3 Order of elements

The elements listed in Section 10.2(a) shall appear in the order set out above. A comma shall separate the repository name from the reference code, and a full stop shall conclude the citation.

Example:

National Archives of Singapore, “Minutes of the Colonial Secretary’s Meetings, 1921–1923,” CO 273/521, f. 14.

10.4 Citations to digital records

(a) Where a record is consulted in digital form, the citation shall include the URL or persistent identifier and the date on which the record was accessed.

(b) Where a record is available only in digital form, the citation shall state that the record is a digital surrogate and, where known, the location of the original.

**3. ACCESS TIERS**

3.1 Access to SAA collections is organised into three tiers:

| Tier | Description | Examples | Registration Required |
|------|-------------|----------|----------------------|
| A | Open access — no registration | Published guides, indexes, publicly available finding aids, exhibition materials | No |
| B | Registered access — reading room use | Original records, microfilm, restricted digital databases | Yes (basic) |
| C | Controlled access — project-based | Records containing personal data, fragile originals, materials subject to donor restrictions | Yes (enhanced, with stated research purpose) |

3.2 Tier B registration is valid for two years from the date of issue. Tier C approvals are valid for a defined project period, not exceeding 12 months, and may be renewed once.

3.3 Applications for Tier C access must be submitted at least seven working days before the intended visit. The Access Review Panel will consider the research purpose, the sensitivity of the material, and the applicant's prior record of compliance.

**4. CLOSED MATERIAL**

4.1 The following categories of records are closed to public access:

a. Records containing personal data of living individuals, unless consent has been obtained or the records are more than 100 years old;

b. Records whose disclosure would prejudice the security of the Republic;

c. Records subject to a donor-imposed restriction;

d. Records whose physical condition makes consultation unsafe, pending conservation treatment.

4.2 The list of closed material is reviewed annually. Researchers may appeal a closure decision in writing to the Assistant Director (Access).

**5. READING ROOM USE**

5.1 Reading room hours are 9:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Mondays to Saturdays, excluding public holidays. The last admission is at 5:00 p.m.

5.2 All bags, briefcases, and personal devices must be deposited in the lockers provided on Level 1 of the Canning Rise building. Lockers are free of charge but require a $2 refundable deposit or a valid SAA access card.

5.3 Pencils and paper are permitted. Pens, markers, and correction fluid are not allowed in the reading room.

5.4 Researchers may request up to six items per visit. Items will be retrieved from the stacks and delivered to the assigned seat within 20 minutes.

5.5 No food or drinks, including capped water bottles, are permitted inside the reading room. A pantry with a water dispenser is located on Level 2, beside the lift lobby.

5.6 Photography of original records is permitted only where the item is not marked as "No Photography" and where flash is not used. Digital cameras and mobile phones may be used for this purpose, provided that the researcher has signed the Photography Agreement (Form PA-3).

**6. DIGITAL ACCESS SERVICES**

6.1 The SAA Online Catalogue is available at the public terminals in the reading room and remotely via the SAA website.

6.2 The following digital collections are available to Tier B researchers without further application:

a. Digitised photographs (pre-1965);

b. Colonial-era government gazettes;

c. Oral history interview summaries (access copies only);

d. Building plans index (metadata only).

6.3 Full audio and video recordings of oral history interviews are available only to Tier C researchers, subject to the conditions attached to each interview.

**8. CITATION AND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT**

8.1 All published work that draws on SAA collections must acknowledge the Singapore Archives Association and cite the specific record reference numbers used.

8.2 The recommended citation format is: “Singapore Archives Association, [record reference], [series title], [date].” Full citation guidance is provided in the SAA Style Sheet for Researchers, available at the reference desk.

8.3 Researchers are required to deposit one copy of any published work that is based substantially on SAA material, within three months of publication. This copy is held for reference use only.

**9. DATA PROTECTION AND PERSONAL INFORMATION**

9.1 Records containing personal data are subject to the Personal Data Protection Act 2012 and to any access restrictions imposed at the time of transfer.

9.2 Researchers who encounter personal information that is not relevant to their stated research purpose must not record, copy, or disclose that information.

9.3 Where a researcher believes that a record contains information that should be restricted under this Protocol, they may flag the item to the Assistant Director (Access) using Form FL-2. The flag does not itself close the record, but prompts a review within 14 working days.

10.1 This Protocol is reviewed annually by the Public Access Working Group. Amendments are made by the Director (Collections) on the recommendation of the Group.

10.3 Approved amendments are published as a revised version of the Protocol. The version number and date of approval are recorded on the cover page.

**2. Scope**
The guidelines apply to all engagement activities organised by SAA, including but not limited to
workshops, exhibitions, heritage trails, school visits, public talks, and digital outreach
initiatives.

**3. Key Principles**
3.1 Engagement should be inclusive and accessible to all members of the community, including
persons with disabilities, seniors, and families with young children.
3.2 Activities should be designed in consultation with community partners and participants where
practicable.
3.3 All engagement should reflect SAA’s commitment to preserving and promoting Singapore’s
archival heritage.

**4. Planning and Approval**
4.1 All engagement activities must be submitted for approval using the standard Activity Proposal
Form (APF-2024).
4.2 Proposals should be submitted at least four weeks before the proposed activity date.
4.3 The Director’s Office will review proposals and provide feedback within five working days.
4.4 Activities requiring significant resources or involving external partners must be endorsed by
the Director before commitment.

**5. Community Partners and Venues**
5.1 SAA welcomes collaboration with schools, grassroots organisations, museums, and other heritage
institutions.
5.2 When selecting venues, preference should be given to accessible locations, including those
near MRT stations or with good bus connectivity.
5.3 For activities held in public spaces such as void decks or community clubs, organisers must
obtain the necessary permits from the relevant authorities.

**6. Communication and Promotion**
6.1 All promotional materials should include the SAA logo and contact details.
6.2 Language used in materials should be clear and simple, with translations provided where
appropriate.
6.3 Digital promotion should be scheduled across SAA’s official social media channels at least
two weeks before the activity.

**7. Evaluation and Reporting**
7.1 Organisers must submit a brief activity report within two weeks of the activity.
7.2 Reports should include participant numbers, feedback received, and lessons learned.
7.3 The Director’s Office will maintain a central log of all engagement activities for annual
review.

9.4 Where a partner requests use of SAA facilities or resources, the Resource Request Form
(RRF-2024) must be completed and approved before the activity is confirmed.

9.5 The Director’s Office will maintain a partner contact list, reviewed annually in January.

**10. Event Calendars**

10.1 The Director’s Office will publish a quarterly calendar of all planned engagement
activities by the first working day of each quarter.

10.2 Staff should update the calendar entry for their activity within three working days of any
change.

10.3 The calendar will be accessible to all staff via the shared drive; external partners will
receive a monthly summary of relevant activities.

10.4 Activities that are still at the proposal stage should be marked as “Planned” and should
not be publicised externally until the proposal is approved.

11.1 Any media release or press invitation must be cleared by the Director’s Office at least
five working days before distribution.

11.2 Staff should not speak to the media on behalf of SAA without prior written authorisation.

11.3 Photography and videography at activities should follow the consent guidelines in Section
5.5.
